content: 1. In tennis, the term set point refers to a situation where a player is one point away from winning a set. 2. In electronics, set point describes the specific value at which an electrical circuit is either activated or deactivated. 3. In medicine, set point refers to a particular value, such as body weight or body temperature, that the body strives to maintain through regulatory mechanisms (a concept closely related to homeostasis). 4. In control systems, setpoint is the desired target value that an automatic control system, such as a PID controller, is programmed to achieve. 5. SetPoint is the name of a driver software suite designed for Logitech computer mice.
